query: Her Own Prescription Sister Amaranth is up a week too soon, grey at the edges, taking the tray out for the evening round as if nothing had happened. At bed two she sways and puts a hand on the rail. {flag(bed_six_truth): Four second-years sit up in their beds to watch.|The whole ward goes quiet.} Everyone looks at you. "Bed." You take the tray out of her hands and say it the way she says it to everyone else. She looks at you for a long moment. Then she goes to bed. You do the round. In the morning there's a card on the tray, in her square hand: "Bed four needs less." Walk the round beside her You don't argue. You carry the tray and have each bottle ready before she reaches for it. At the last bed she sits down on the end of it, and lets you measure out her own dose. "Half a spoon," she says. "I'm not a horse."
